import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Handle missing Income values by dropping rows where Income is NaN
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# Calculate 'Total_Spending' by summing all 'Mnt' (amount spent) columns
spending_cols = [col for col in df.columns if col.startswith('Mnt')]
df['Total_Spending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Filter out extreme outliers for better visualization clarity
# For Income: remove values above the 99th percentile
df_filtered = df[df['Income'] < df['Income'].quantile(0.99)]
# For Total_Spending: remove values above the 99th percentile
df_filtered = df_filtered[df_filtered['Total_Spending'] < df_filtered['Total_Spending'].quantile(0.99)]


# Set up the matplotlib figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a scatter plot of Total Spending vs. Income, colored by Education level
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_filtered,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    hue='Education',
    palette='viridis',  # A perceptually uniform colormap
    alpha=0.7,          # Transparency to help with overplotting
    s=70                # Marker size
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Total Customer Spending vs. Income by Education Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Income (€)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending (€)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to avoid overlapping with data points
plt.legend(title='Education Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Ensure all elements fit within the figure area
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
